The dining scene in Des Moines is pretty hot these days.
So why did nearly a thousand Iowans part with $100 apiece last Saturday night to sit through what was, at best, a culinary and social experiment known as the Jefferson-Jackson Dinner?
For many, the event marked another iteration of what has become a beloved (if expensive) tradition in Iowa’s political landscape.
The annual Jefferson-Jackson Dinner, hosted by the Iowa Democratic Party, is as much a spectacle of pageantry as it is a celebration of democracy.

The dinner’s ostensible purpose is to showcase the Iowa Democratic caucus’s unity ahead of the presidential primary season—but the experience for attendees tends to be more about tradition and theatrics than the food itself.

Guests arrived at the Drake University's Palmer House under a canopy of lanterns and banners, their meals featuring a bewildering assortment of home-cooked fare—think wilted salads, rubbery chicken, and the infamous “zombie burger”—all passed around family-style with little explanation.

Photographers and TV crews swarmed the long table, and members of the party’s national and state leadership took turns in a carefully choreographed procession, offering platitudes about “unity” and “progress.”

For those paying the $100 cover charge (often in addition to drink prices), the night was less about the cuisine and more about the ritual: shaking hands with state officials, hearing a series of speeches in which the same talking points were repeated with ever-greater gravitas, and watching the crowd don traditional party sashes as they snapped a collective photo for their social media feeds.

sentences.sentence: Russia was accused of sending tanks into Ukraine for the first time yesterday while the West’s attention was diverted by the chaos in Iraq.
The development threatens to destroy the tentative peace process just when the US and EU had hoped Vladimir Putin had agreed to ease tensions following recent diplomatic breakthroughs.

Interior Minister Arseny Avakov of Ukraine made the allegation during a press briefing, stating that Ukrainian forces observed armored vehicles—including tanks—crossing into the country via a checkpoint in the Luhansk region.
The checkpoint is currently under the de facto control of pro-Russian separatists, who have long held parts of eastern Ukraine, mainly in the Russian-speaking region.
The pro-separatists, widely backed by Russia, have controlled several towns and cities in the northeast of the country since 2014, prompting international concern over Moscow’s influence.

Despite repeated denials, Russian authorities have not commented directly on the specific incident, but the timing comes amid widespread skepticism about Putin’s promises to curtail military support to separatist groups.

Russian officials have insisted that their state has “no involvement” in the activities of separatist forces in Ukraine, a stance that Western analysts have viewed with skepticism given the history of past interventions.
President Vladimir Putin has promised to tighten border controls in Russia, perhaps in response to international pressure over the conflict.

sentences.sentence: It’s set to be one of the most groundbreaking moments in humanity’s six decades of space exploration: Today SpaceX was due to land a Falcon 9 rocket on a floating platform after launching a Dragon capsule.
But those looking forward to this pivotal moment will have to wait a little.
The launch, originally scheduled for today at Cape Canaveral, Florida, was delayed once again after engineers discovered a problem with one of the Falcon 9’s Raptor engines.
This recurring issue—a faulty or underperforming engine—first pushed back the launch from earlier in the week.
Now, SpaceX has pushed the launch to Tuesday, January 6th at 11:18 AM GMT (around 4:18 PM EST).
The Falcon 9’s first stage, loaded with the NASA-awarded Dragon cargo capsule, was set to blast off carrying critical supplies to the International Space Station.
However, the main goal today was to attempt the first-ever vertical landing of the rocket’s first stage on a specially positioned ocean barge.
This marks a major leap for SpaceX’s vision of fully reusable rockets, a core part of its strategy to drastically reduce the cost of space travel.
If successful, the engine-powered booster would return to land for a vertical touchdown—something that, until today, had only been attempted with aircraft and some experimental rockets.
CEO Elon Musk has previously stated the landing has about a 50% chance of success, reflecting the technological boldness and engineering challenges involved.
Despite the setback, this mission represents a critical step toward Musk’s ultimate goal: making all SpaceX rockets reusable.

sentences.sentence: One investigative tip can lead to another -- and another.
Linda Abrams, a self-described “genealogy gumshoe,” began her latest search in Texas, hoping to connect the dots surrounding the infamous crew of the Confederate submarine H.L.

What started as a comparison of historical handwriting samples for a local museum display soon became a pursuit through the ages to solve the lingering mysteries of the crew’s fate during the Civil War.
Abrams’s interest in the Hunley was piqued not long after she learned about a recent discovery of the long-lost submarine off the coast of South Carolina in 2000.
The Hunley became famous not for surviving, but for vanishing—along with its entire eight-man crew—just a day after attacking a Union ship.
Of those eight men, nearly nothing was known about their identities or backgrounds until a decade ago, when DNA partially identified one: Paul Walshe, a Confederate sailor from South Carolina.
But as the genetic puzzle grew, so too did the gaps.
Was there any way to fill in the missing pieces?
That question led Abrams, armed with genealogical databases and forensic methods, to dig even deeper.
Her investigation took a turn when Abrams received a tip in Kentucky, apparently from someone claiming to know details about one of the crew members.
Rather than dismiss it, she traveled to the state, careful to verify each lead.
She spent weeks poring over census records and military logs, cross-referencing names, physical descriptions, and familial ties.
But each time she followed a promising thread, it dissolved into hearsay or dead ends.

sentences.sentence: CNN anchor is causing a stir over his vulgar Twitter tirade against rival network Fox News.

Bill Weir, who joined CNN from ABC News last fall, lashed out publicly over a Fox Nation headline mocking climate change and former Vice President Al Gore during coverage of the EPA hearings in Denver.

On Wednesday, Weir took to Twitter in response to Fox Nation’s piece titled, “Climate Doesn’t Cooperate With Al Gore’s Group’s Visit to Denver EPA Hearings.” In his tweet, Weir expressed his annoyance, writing, “If this is what passes for journalism these days, maybe Fox News should stick to reality or at least get a better fact-checker.” The initial tweet quickly drew criticism for its pointed language and what some described as unnecessarily personal and crude remarks.
Before long, Weir issued an apology for what he called “an unprofessional moment,” acknowledging that his comment crossed a line.
However, in an unexpected move, he chose not to delete his initial Tweet, sparking further debate online about the boundaries of public discourse and professional conduct for news personalities.

sentences.sentence: Police in Rotherham have come under fire for holding a self-congratulatory awards ceremony just two weeks after a damning report accused the force of failing to protect vulnerable children who were sexually abused in the town.
A gala event was hosted at Rotherham United’s stadium, where South Yorkshire Police leaders boasted about officers who went “beyond the call of duty” in their work.
The ceremony was attended by senior figures from the force and local officials, during which awards were presented for bravery and service.
However, the timing of the event has raised serious questions about the force’s priorities.

The revelations came only days after the release of a widely critiqued report from the Independent Office for Police and Crime Commission (IOPC), which exposed serious failures in safeguarding practices and leadership at South Yorkshire Police.
The report found that children in Rotherham were at significant risk for years before some were finally reported to authorities.

In the wake of these revelations, critics have argued that the police force should be focused on addressing systemic failures and improving protection for the most at-risk individuals rather than celebrating individual acts of heroism.
The timing has also prompted calls for greater transparency and accountability within the police service.
Local police and crime commissioner for Rotherham, who attended the awards, defended the event as a way to boost morale and recognition among staff.

sentences.sentence: New Zealanders Danica and Paul Weekes are no strangers to disaster.
The couple’s eldest son, Lincoln, was born in the midst of an earthquake in Christchurch in 2010.

Just over three years later, in December 2014, tragedy struck again when their son, along with 227 other passengers and crew, disappeared without a trace on Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 while en route from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing.

Now, as the search continues with no definitive answers nearly a decade later, the Weeks family, like so many others, remains eternally anxious, waiting desperately for any news or sign that their loved ones might have survived or, at least, been laid to rest.

Every hour without a confirmed update only deepens the pain and uncertainty for families scattered around the globe—each clinging to hope, memories, and fragile messages of hope shared through social media and online tributes.
Notable among the missing was martial arts star Ju Kun, a Chinese actor who was en route to Hollywood at the time of the disaster.
His sudden absence stunned the international martial arts community, with tributes pouring in from fans who admired his skill and charisma.
The global impact of his loss resonated widely, as countless social media posts and online flowers of memory illuminated the depth of his influence and the sorrow his family felt.

Communities from various corners of the world are holding vigils and prayer meetings in the hope that the flight’s wreckage might one day be found, or that a breakthrough in the ongoing investigations could bring closure to grieving families.

sentences.sentence: The sister of a man suspected in the shooting of Pakistani activist Malala Yousufzai has issued a statement of remorse after the attack that sparked global outrage and concern.

The 23-year-old suspect, often identified online as Atta Ullah, is currently wanted by authorities in connection with the October 2012 assault that left the then-15-year-old Malala gravely wounded for advocating girls' education in Swat Valley.
Rehana Haleem, the sister of Atta Ullah, broke her long silence today with a message intended for Malala.
"Please convey a message to Malala, that I apologize for what my brother did to her," Haleem said.
"He has brought shame on our family.
I don't consider Atta Ullah my brother any more."
Haleem’s words came as the international community continued to call for justice and healing following the incident, which shook the world and became a symbol of courage against extremism.

Her apology stands in stark contrast to previous statements attributed to her family during the aftermath of the attack, reflecting a complex and painful evolution of sentiment within the family in the years since the shooting.

Naval sources later confirmed that the Charles de Gaulle is now fully deployed in the region and will participate in a range of missions for several weeks.

According to the latest tallies, the vast majority of those killed are suspected ISIS militants.
However, there were 62 civilian casualties among the total, underscoring the ongoing risks of the conflict for non-military populations in the region.
French officials have indicated that the Charles de Gaulle’s aircraft will join with those of allied forces in support operations, including airstrikes and logistical support.
The French carrier is considered a key element in Europe’s efforts to combat ISIS, providing flexible air power in the challenging Iraqi environment.

French Defense Minister Florence Parly earlier expressed solidarity with the Iraqi people and emphasized that the French operation would be conducted within the framework of international law and the United Nations resolutions.
